B0200.d: B0200 is not documented in public: no publicly available J2012 list and no carmaker uses it with this meaning. What the title describes is real.
s: Airbag warning lamp on, sometimes only after a cold start or jump start
Other modules may also log low-voltage faults
Safety note: airbags may not deploy while the fault is present; work on the system only with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed
c: high
Weak battery or charging fault letting system voltage sag, often while cranking
medium
Poor ground or loose supply pin at the airbag control unit connector, or a corroded fuse contact
low
Airbag control unit faulty, for example its internal supply or reserve capacitor

B0205.d: B0205 is absent from the published J2012 lists, and no carmaker documents it for the defroster door; a defrost door circuit has the code B0278. Saab files its 9-3 defrost door motor under B0240 06 and B0241 01, where an open, grounded or B+ shorted motor circuit leads to wrong air distribution.
s: Little or no air reaches the windscreen in defrost mode
Air comes from the wrong outlets or a clicking noise is heard behind the dashboard
c: high
Defroster door actuator with stripped gears or worn feedback potentiometer
medium
Door or linkage binding, broken or blocked by foreign objects
low
Position feedback or reference wire open or shorted

B0210.d: No publicly available J2012 table mentions B0210, and no carmaker documents it; lost or invalid communication with a rain sensing module is covered by U0231 and U0532. The sensor is mounted behind the windscreen, inside the car and within the wiped area.
s: Automatic wiping does not react to rain or wipes on a dry screen
Wipers only work in fixed interval or manual stages
Automatic headlamps may also stop working on combined rain/light sensors
c: high
Gel pad aged or with air bubbles, often after a windscreen replacement
medium
Rain sensor electronics failed or moisture inside the housing
low
Supply or data wire to the sensor at the headliner damaged

B0220.d: B0220 is absent from the openly accessible J2012 lists and from carmaker documents, so it cannot be proven publicly; the front wiper motor circuit itself has the code B0900. The speed circuit is the part that selects slow or fast wiping.
s: Wipers work at only one speed, slow or fast
Wipers run at one speed and cannot be switched to the other
c: high
High/low speed relay or its contacts failed in the fuse box or control module
medium
Wire or plug to the low or high speed brush of the motor open or shorted
medium
One speed brush worn out or burnt inside the wiper motor

B0223.d: B0223 does not appear in the publicly available J2012 lists, but General Motors uses it for the recirculation door actuator. On GM Global A cars such as the Saab 9-5 and 9-4X of model year 2011 that actuator is a stepper motor with four control lines; B0223 01 means command circuit 1 is shorted to battery, B0223 06 that it is open or low.
s: Recirculation cannot be switched on or off
Windows mist up or outside smells get in because the door is stuck
c: high
Recirculation door stepper motor faulty or its gears stripped
medium
Control line 1 to the actuator open, grounded or shorted to battery voltage
low
HVAC control module software, as in GM bulletin PIT5383A, or module output stage

B0226.d: The publicly available J2012 lists have no B0226, and no maker documents it for headlamp levelling. Saab uses the number in its 9-3 climate control: B0226 01 is a short to B+ in the recirculation motor circuit, possibly causing stale air or misted windows.
s: Headlamp levelling warning shown and beam height no longer adjusts
Oncoming drivers flash because the beam is set too high under load
c: high
Lever or coupling rod of the front axle sensor bent, broken or detached
medium
Connector or wire at the sensor corroded or damaged by road splash
medium
Sensor worn out internally or not calibrated after replacement or suspension work

B0228.d: B0228 appears in none of the publicly available J2012 lists, and no carmaker publishes it as a fog lamp code. General Motors does use the number, but inside climate control: bulletin PIT5383 lists B0228 among the HVAC codes of 2015 Cadillac, Chevrolet and GMC models whose K33 climate module needed new software; GM does not publish its exact wording.
s: Front fog lamps stay dark although the switch is on
Fog lamp indicator lights up but only one lamp or none works
c: high
Fog lamp relay or fuse failed, so the lamps get no supply although the switch is on
medium
Low-mounted harness in the front bumper torn or corroded, often after a parking knock or water ingress
medium
Bulb burnt out or lamp housing flooded through a cracked lens
low
Fog position of the light switch worn or its signal line open

B0231.d: B0231 is found neither in any publicly available J2012 list nor in public service documents of a carmaker, so the code cannot be verified. The title points to the front marker or position lamps.
s: One front marker or position lamp stays dark with parking lights on
Bulb failure warning in the instrument cluster, where the car has one
c: high
Bulb or LED module of the marker lamp failed
medium
Corroded bulb holder or plug in the headlamp area, where spray water reaches it
low
Feed or ground wire to the front lamp open or shorted

B0233.d: Public J2012 listings leave B0233 out, yet GM assigns it in its Global A climate control for the air distribution (mode) actuator. On 2011 Saab 9-5 and 9-4X cars that actuator is a stepper motor: the HVAC module feeds it a 12 V reference and switches its four coils to ground in pulses.
s: Air comes from the wrong outlets and the selected distribution is ignored
Windscreen cannot be demisted because air will not switch to defrost
c: high
Mode stepper actuator failed internally, e.g. a burnt coil or worn gear
medium
One of the four control lines or the 12 V reference chafed, open or shorted behind the dash
low
HVAC module software fault on affected GM models, fixed by reprogramming

B0235.d: No publicly available J2012 list contains B0235, nor does any carmaker describe it, which leaves it unverified; side-specific brake lamp codes are B0850 and B0851. Stop lamps send a steady red signal rearward while the driver brakes, and FMVSS 108 also demands a third stop lamp mounted high.
s: One or more brake lamps stay dark when the pedal is pressed
Bulb warning shown, sometimes together with traction or stability warning lamps
Safety note: following traffic gets no braking signal; repair before further driving
c: high
Stop lamp bulb or LED unit failed
medium
Brake light switch misadjusted, worn or wet inside
medium
Blown fuse or broken wire, often in the tailgate or boot lid harness
low
Corroded lamp holder or plug in the rear light cluster

B0237.d: Neither the publicly available J2012 lists nor any public service literature mention B0237, so it remains unconfirmed. In the words of FMVSS 108, backup lamps light the road behind the car and warn pedestrians and drivers that it is reversing or about to.
s: Reversing lamps stay dark with reverse gear engaged
Reversing lamps lit while driving forward
c: high
Reverse light switch on the gearbox worn or its plug corroded by road spray
medium
Reversing lamp bulb burnt out or LED unit failed
low
Missing reverse signal from the range sensor or transmission module on automatics
low
Broken wire in the tailgate harness feeding the lamp

B0239.d: B0239 cannot be traced in any J2012 source or factory document, so its use stays unproven; the same title belongs to B0860. The licence plate lamp lights the rear registration plate and is usually wired with the tail lamps.
s: Rear number plate is not lit with the lights on
Bulb warning in the cluster, where the car monitors this lamp
c: high
Plate lamp bulb or LED unit failed, often from water inside the housing
medium
Wire broken in the flexible tube between body and tailgate or boot lid
low
Retrofitted LED lamp not matched by the body module coding

B0240.d: Searching J2012 sources turned up no B0240, and no maker applies it to the headlamp switch; the identical title belongs to B0800. Saab gives the number another job: in the 9-3 climate system B0240 06 means the defrost door motor circuit is open or grounded, with wrong air distribution as a result, and B0241 01 that this motor is shorted to B+.
s: Lights do not follow the switch position or fall back to a fixed setting
Automatic lights or parking lights cannot be selected
c: high
Worn or dirty contacts or resistor track inside the light switch
medium
Switch plug loose or corroded behind the dashboard trim
low
Signal line to the body module shorted to ground or supply

B0245.d: B0245 is unknown to every publicly available J2012 source and undocumented by carmakers, so nothing public backs it; driver window faults have the code B0500. The driver's door usually holds the master switch block, which commands its own window and, by signal lines or a bus, the other doors.
s: Driver's window or other windows do not respond to the master switch
A window moves on its own or the one-touch function misbehaves
c: high
Master switch contacts corroded or sticking, often after drinks or rain got into the door panel
medium
Wires broken in the rubber boot between body and driver's door
low
Plug of the switch block loose or with pushed-back pins

B0247.d: B0247 is listed in none of the publicly available J2012 sources and no carmaker publishes it; passenger window circuit faults have the code B0501. The passenger switch is the simpler partner of the driver's master block: it moves only its own window, and the master can override it or lock it out.
s: Passenger window works from the driver's switch but not from its own
Passenger switch moves the window only in one direction
c: high
Passenger window switch worn or contaminated
medium
Signal line between passenger door and master switch broken at the door hinge
low
Window lock button on the master stuck or its circuit faulty

B0250.d: None of the publicly available J2012 lists contain B0250. On the Saab 9-3 the number marks an actuator fault instead: B0250 06 means the floor door motor circuit is open or grounded, which upsets air distribution, while B0251 01 is the B+ short.
s: Automatic climate control holds the wrong cabin temperature
Blower speed and outlet temperature no longer adapt as the cabin warms up
c: high
Sensor plug or wiring behind the dashboard open or shorted to ground
medium
NTC element in the sensor damaged
low
Aspirator fan seized or its intake grille blocked, so the reading lags behind cabin temperature

B0252.d: For B0252 there is neither a J2012 entry nor any factory description, so the code is unverified. The title names one direction of the driver's window motor.
s: Driver's window closes but will not go down
Pinch protection or one-touch down no longer works
c: high
Down relay contact or driver transistor in the door module burnt
medium
One motor lead broken in the door or at the motor plug
low
Worn motor brushes or commutator with a dead spot in one direction

B0255.d: B0255 shows up in no publicly available J2012 source. Saab's 9-3 uses it for a door motor: B0255 06 reports the right vent door motor circuit open or grounded, B0256 01 the B+ short on that motor.
s: Outside temperature display shows dashes or an implausible value
Automatic climate control regulates poorly, especially in cold or hot weather
c: high
Outside sensor broken by stone impact or corroded by road salt
medium
Sensor wiring behind the bumper pinched or torn, often after front-end repairs
low
Moisture in the sensor plug changing the measured resistance

B0258.d: The public J2012 sources do not list B0258, and no carmaker documents it publicly; it cannot be verified. GM's Global A system logs its left, or main, temperature actuator under B0408 instead, as the 2011 Saab 9-5 manual shows.
s: Air from the vents stays hot or cold whatever temperature is set
Clicking or knocking behind the dashboard when the temperature is changed
c: high
Blend door actuator motor or its feedback potentiometer failed
medium
Actuator plug or wires under the dashboard loose, chafed or shorted
low
Door jammed by debris or a broken shaft, overloading the motor drive

B0260.d: No publicly available J2012 list contains B0260 with this meaning, and the same title belongs to B0970. Saab uses the number in the climate control of the 2003 9-3: B0260 06 stands for the left vent door motor circuit open or grounded, B0261 01 for a short to B+.
s: Interior lamps do not come on when a door opens
Interior lamps stay lit or the battery is flat after the car stood overnight
c: high
Door contact switch or lock contact sticking, so the module sees a door open
medium
Lamp feed shorted in the roof liner or a lamp unit with water damage
low
Battery saver relay or output stage in the body module faulty

B0263.d: B0263 shares the fate of its sibling B0258: no publicly available J2012 source lists it and no maker describes it. The second blend door usually serves the passenger side or the rear zone.
s: Passenger side or rear outlets stay at one temperature whatever is set
Noticeable temperature difference between left and right outlets
c: high
Passenger-side or rear blend actuator failed
medium
Wiring to the second actuator open or shorted, often near the centre console
low
Shared linkage or door shaft broken, overloading the drive

B0265.d: Nothing in the publicly available J2012 sources or carmaker literature mentions B0265, so it is unverifiable; related codes are B0270 and B0272. The lock/unlock button in the driver's door tells the body or door module to run all lock motors, as HELLA's overview of central locking describes.
s: Doors cannot be locked or unlocked with the interior button
Locks cycle on their own or ignore the remote key
c: high
Lock/unlock button sticking or shorted by moisture in the door panel
medium
Switch wires broken in the boot between body and driver's door
low
Input stage in the body or door module damaged

B0268.d: B0268 is not in the published J2012 lists, but General Motors uses the number: bulletin PIP5094, written for 2014 and older GM cars and light trucks, includes it in its keyword list of body codes, without a descriptor. The mode door routes air to face vents, footwell or windscreen.
s: Air stays on one outlet, for example defrost, whatever mode is chosen
Pressing the mode button no longer changes where the air comes out
c: high
Mode door actuator motor or position feedback failed
medium
Actuator over-travelling or binding at the door, overloading its drive
low
Actuator plug or wiring behind the dash open or shorted

B0270.d: Public evidence for B0270 is lacking: it is absent from every publicly available J2012 list, and no manufacturer describes it. The title points to the lock/unlock rocker in the front passenger door.
s: Passenger door lock button has no effect on central locking
Doors lock or unlock by themselves when the switch line is shorted
Remote key and driver switch still lock the car normally
c: high
Lock rocker in the passenger door worn, sticking or contaminated
medium
Switch signal wire chafed to ground or broken in the door hinge passage
medium
Water ingress or corrosion at the door trim switch connector
low
Door or body control module input stage faulty

B0272.d: Neither the reachable J2012 lists nor any carmaker's documents mention B0272, which leaves the code unproven. Its title covers the interior central-locking button in general, without naming a door.
s: Interior lock button does not lock or unlock the doors
Locks cycle unexpectedly or only react to the remote key
c: high
Central-locking button mechanically stuck or contacts worn
medium
Switch wire shorted to ground or open between switch and module
low
Spilled liquid or condensation in the switch panel
low
Door or body control module misreads the switch input

B0273.d: B0273 could not be traced in the code lists at hand, nor in any manufacturer publication. The title concerns the electrical circuit of the actuator that swings the intake door between outside air and cabin air.
s: Recirculation button changes nothing at the air intake
Windows fog up or outside odours enter the cabin
Reduced cooling on hot days
c: high
Recirculation door actuator motor burnt out or internally open
medium
Actuator wiring behind the glovebox chafed, shorted or unplugged
low
Door jammed by leaves or debris so the motor stalls at high current
low
Driver stage in the climate control module defective

B0274.d: Nothing public confirms B0274 – the publicly available J2012 tables skip it and no maker explains it. The title refers to the switch the driver or a passer-by uses to release the boot lid electrically.
s: Boot lid cannot be opened with the button, only by key or remote
Lid unlatches without anyone pressing the button
c: high
Exterior release button corroded or full of water and dirt
medium
Wires broken in the flexible boot lid hinge loom
medium
Interior release button held or jammed by trim
low
Door or body module input reading the switch defective

B0278.d: B0278 appears neither in J2012 tables nor in factory service material, so its existence is open. By its title it covers the electrical side of the defrost door actuator, the flap that routes air to the windscreen.
s: Windscreen clears slowly because little air reaches it
Air keeps blowing at the windscreen whatever mode is selected
c: high
Defrost door actuator motor open or shorted internally
medium
Actuator wiring under the dashboard damaged or connector loose
low
Door or linkage seized so the motor draws excessive current
low
Actuator driver in the climate control module failed

B0283.d: B0283 is not in any publicly available J2012 list; it is documented by Saab/GM, where it means the heated rear window relay, not a blower. In the Saab 9-3 (2003–2012) the rear electrical centre sets B0283 01 when the relay output exceeds 6 V with heating on, and B0283 06 when it stays below 6 V (open or grounded line).
s: Heated rear window does not work when switched on
Rear window heats continuously and cannot be switched off
Battery drained if the grid keeps heating
c: high
Rear window heater relay with open coil or welded contacts
medium
Relay control wire open, grounded or shorted to battery voltage
medium
Poor ground or corroded socket at the relay
low
Output stage of the climate or electrical centre module faulty

B0288.d: A search found B0288 in no J2012 list and in no carmaker's service data; it stays unconfirmed. The refrigerant pressure sensor it names sits on the high-pressure line; its signal decides whether the compressor may run and how fast the cooling fan turns.
s: Air conditioning blows warm because the compressor is disabled
Radiator fan runs constantly or at the wrong speed
c: high
Refrigerant pressure sensor failed or signal drifting
medium
Sensor connector near the condenser corroded by road spray
medium
5 V reference, ground or signal wire open or shorted
low
Very low refrigerant charge giving an implausible reading

B0290.d: B0290 has no public source: the publicly available J2012 tables omit it, and service literature is silent. The title names the push button that requests the heated rear window.
s: Pressing the rear defrost button has no effect
Rear window heating switches on by itself or cannot be cancelled
Indicator lamp in the button stays dark or lit
c: high
Rear defrost button contacts worn or button stuck in the panel
medium
Climate control faceplate or its circuit board defective
low
Signal or data line between panel and module interrupted

B0292.d: Whether B0292 is used anywhere is unknown; no consulted J2012 list carries it and no maker documents it. Its title points to the electromagnetic clutch that couples a belt-driven compressor to its pulley, and the relay feeding the clutch coil.
s: No cooling, compressor hub does not turn with A/C on
Compressor runs permanently even with A/C switched off
c: high
Clutch coil open or shorted, often after overheating
medium
A/C clutch relay failed or contacts welded
medium
Excessive clutch air gap so the plate does not pull in
low
Clutch feed or ground wire at the compressor damaged by heat
